title: A Tornado Hit 302 mph. It's the Fastest Wind Ever Measured on Earth

scenes.text: In 1999, a tornado hit 302 miles an hour. The fastest wind ever measured.
Bridge Creek, Oklahoma. A radar truck caught the number from a few miles away.
The wind picked up a 36,000 pound freight car and threw it three quarters of a mile.
Houses bolted to concrete were swept away. Only the slabs were left.
The funnel was a mile wide and stayed on the ground for 38 miles.
Highway speed limits top out around 80. This was nearly four of them at once.

description:
On May 3, 1999, a Doppler on Wheels radar measured winds of about 302 miles an hour inside the Bridge Creek tornado in Oklahoma, the fastest wind speed ever recorded on Earth.
The F5 tornado threw a 36,000 pound freight car three quarters of a mile and swept bolted-down houses off their foundations, leaving only concrete slabs.
What is the strongest wind you have ever stood in?
first_comment: The radar reading has an uncertainty of about 20 mph, and a 2021 re-analysis put it even higher. Have you ever seen a tornado with your own eyes?
